findings.title: Global view permission bypasses client-specific denials
findings.body: Granting view on the synthetic Clients resource makes canView() return true, so this branch succeeds without evaluating the target client's permissions. A client-specific negative view permission therefore cannot exclude that client from an all-clients view grant, unlike V2's resource-specific override behavior demonstrated by the user permission tests. Delegated administrators can read explicitly excluded clients. Only built-in admin roles should bypass the per-client evaluation; the all-clients permission should be a fallback.

findings.title: Type-based enumeration misses individual client permission resources
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates individual client resources with a name and scopes but does not assign their type. Only the synthetic Clients resource receives the Clients type during initialization. Consequently, findByType cannot enumerate individual client grants: getClientsWithPermission returns an empty set for client-specific permissions and can return the literal "Clients" for a global permission instead of client IDs. Consumers using this set to filter accessible clients receive incorrect results.

findings.title: Provision the new schema entries for already-enabled realms
findings.body: The new Clients resource and scopes are provisioned only when init creates the admin-permissions client, but init immediately returns when that client already exists. A realm initialized with the previous Users-only schema therefore never receives the Clients resource or the configure/map-roles-client-scope/map-roles-composite scopes. Creating an individual client permission then fails because getOrCreateResource tries to attach all Clients scopes and throws "No scopes found." for the missing entries. Existing resource servers need their schema reconciled rather than being skipped.

findings.title: Handle client deletion for V2 permission resources
findings.body: When V2 is enabled without the legacy feature, this guard skips ClientRemovedEvent handling entirely, and no V2 cleanup is added. Individual V2 client resources are owned by the admin-permissions client and merely use the target client's UUID as their name, so deleting the target client does not remove those resources through ownership cleanup. Deleting a client with V2 permissions leaves dangling authorization resources and permission associations. Add a V2 removal path instead of ignoring the event.

findings.title: Resolve resource labels for Clients permissions
findings.body: Clients resources are now supported, but getResourceName still handles only Users and otherwise returns resource.getDisplayName(). Neither individual client resource creation nor initialization of the synthetic Clients resource sets a display name. The resolver therefore returns null for Clients permission resources instead of a client identifier or an "All clients" label, leaving resource labels missing in permission representations. Add Clients name resolution alongside the existing Users handling.
